Rashi on Pesachim 93b:10:1.english: Modi'im - [This is] the name of the city.

Rashi on Pesachim 93b:10:2.hebrew: נקוד על ה' - שברחוקה, וכל ניקוד למעט הדבר בא, דמשמע סמיוה להא תיבה מהכא:
Rashi on Pesachim 93b:10:2.english: Dotted over the heh - [That is, the heh] in [the word] reḥoka ["distant"]; and every dot comes to limit the matter, for it implies: erase this word from here.

Rashi on Pesachim 93b:11:1.hebrew: חמשה עשר מילין - מדקרי ליה תנא דידן דרך רחוקה לגבי פסח, וסבירא ליה לעולא דרך רחוקה — כל שאינו יכול ליכנס בשעת שחיטה, כל שעת שחיטה מהלך ואינו מגיע. ושעת שחיטה מחצות היום ואילך, דבין הערבים כתיב ביה כתמיד. ותמיד, אע"פ שנשחט בשש ומחצה, זמנו מן התורה מתחלת שבע ואילך, שמתחלת החמה להתעקם כלפי מערב קצת ומשחרי כותלי, דהכי אמרינן ביומא בפ' שלישי (דף כח:): צלותיה דאברהם מכי משחרי כותלי, והיינו מחצות היום ולהלן. ופרכינן עלה מהא דתנן: תמיד נשחט בשש ומחצה, ומשני: שאני כותלי בית המקדש, דלא מכווני, רחבם מתחתיהן, ולא משחרי בעיקום פורתא עד חצי שבע. ומיהו, זמן שחיטה מתחלת שבע ואילך, ונמשך עד שתשקע החמה; ומשתשקע החמה לא, דדם נפסל בשקיעת החמה באיזהו מקומן (זבחים דף נו.). ומחצות ועד שקיעת החמה מהלך חמשה עשר מילין, כי הא דר' יוחנן:
Rashi on Pesachim 93b:11:1.english: Fifteen mil - Since our Tanna calls it a "distant road" with respect to the Paschal offering, and Ulla holds [that] a "distant road" [means] anyone who cannot enter [Jerusalem] at the time of slaughter — [that is,] he walks the entire time of slaughter and does not arrive. And the time of slaughter is from midday onward, for "toward evening" is written regarding it, like the daily offering [tamid]. And the daily offering, even though it is slaughtered at six and a half [hours], its time by Torah law is from the beginning of the seventh [hour] onward, when the sun begins to incline slightly toward the west and the walls darken [with shadows] — for so we say in Yoma in the third chapter (28b): Abraham's prayer is from when the walls darken, which is from midday onward. And we raise an objection against this from that which we learned in a Mishnah: "The daily offering is slaughtered at six and a half [hours]," and it answers: The walls of the Temple are different, for they are not perpendicular, [as] their width is at their base, and they do not darken with a slight inclination [of the sun] until halfway through the seventh [hour]. However, the time of slaughter is from the beginning of the seventh [hour] onward, and it extends until the sun sets; and once the sun sets, no, for the blood is disqualified at sunset, [as taught] in [chapter] Eizehu Mekoman (Zevachim 56a). And from midday until sunset one walks fifteen mil, like this [statement] of Rabbi Yochanan.

Rashi on Pesachim 93b:11:3.hebrew: כמה מהלך אדם - בינוני, וביום בינוני דתקופת ניסן ותשרי, שהימים והלילות שוין:
Rashi on Pesachim 93b:11:3.english: How [far is] a person's walk - An average [person], and on an average day of the equinox of Nisan and Tishrei, when the days and the nights are equal.

Rashi on Pesachim 93b:11:5.hebrew: מעלות השחר עד הנץ החמה חמשה מיל - כך שהיית החמה לצאת בעוביו של רקיע, וכנגדה שוהה בשקיעתה ליכנס, דהיינו משקיעתה ועד צאת הכוכבים:
Rashi on Pesachim 93b:11:5.english: From dawn until sunrise is five mil - Such is the time the sun takes to emerge through the thickness of the firmament, and correspondingly it tarries at its setting to enter [it], which is from its setting until the emergence of the stars.

Rashi on Pesachim 93b:11:6.english: Thirty [mil] remain - From [the sun's] rising until its setting.

Rashi on Pesachim 93b:11:7.hebrew: לאורתא - לשקיעת החמה, דשוב אין זמן שחיטה, דדם קדשים נפסל בשקיעת החמה, כדאמרינן באיזהו מקומן בשחיטת קדשים:
Rashi on Pesachim 93b:11:7.english: Until evening - Until sunset, for there is no longer time for slaughtering, since the blood of consecrated [offerings] becomes disqualified at sunset, as we say in [chapter] Eizehu Mekoman in [tractate] Shechitat Kodashim [Zevachim].

Rashi on Pesachim 93b:14:1.hebrew: בשעת אכילה - כל שעת אכילה, שרחוק מחצות היום כל כך שאינו יכול ליכנס כל הלילה. אכילת הפסח כל הלילה, ורבנן עבוד הרחקה ואמור עד חצות לר"ע, ולר"א דאורייתא עד חצות, בפרק בתרא (דף קכ:) ובברכות בפ"ק (דף ט.):
Rashi on Pesachim 93b:14:1.english: During the time of the eating - All of the time of eating — that he is so far away from midday that he cannot enter [Jerusalem] all night. [For] the eating of the Paschal lamb is [permitted] all night [by Torah law], and the Rabbis made a safeguard and said [that it may be eaten only] until midnight, according to Rabbi Akiva; whereas according to Rabbi Elazar [ben Azariah], by Torah law [it is only] until midnight — [as stated] in the last chapter (120b) and in Berakhot in the first chapter (9a).

Rashi on Pesachim 93b:16:1.hebrew: ולרב יהודה קשיא - דאמר כל שאינו יכול ליכנס בשעת אכילה הוא דפטור, הא איחזי למיכל לאורתא חייב:
Rashi on Pesachim 93b:16:1.english: And according to Rav Yehuda it is difficult - For he said [that] it is [only] one who is unable to enter [Jerusalem] at the time of eating who is exempt; hence, [if] he is fit to eat [it] in the evening, he is obligated.

Rashi on Pesachim 93b:16:2.english: Yet [with regard to] one who is ritually impure [from] a creeping animal, etc. - And their dispute is in the chapter [entitled] HaIsha (above, Pesachim 90b).

Rashi on Pesachim 93b:17:1.hebrew: לדידי לא קשיא - דאף על גב דדרך רחוקה פטרנא להאי דחזי לאורתא, ומיחייבנא ליה גבי טמא שרץ, היינו טעמא: דדרך רחוקה תלא רחמנא פטורא דטהור, והיינו דרך רחוקה שאין יכול ליכנס בשעת שחיטה, דגבי עשייה כתיב; ואף על גב דיכול ליכנס בשעת אכילה, רחמנא פטריה. אבל לטמא, לא תלה רחמנא פטורא דידיה בדרך רחוקה אלא בטומאה; וטעמא דטומאה משום אכילה היא ולאו משום עשיה, דהא יכול לשלח קרבנותיו. ועוד, מדכתב טמא נפש ולא כתב בעל קרי או טמא שרץ, שמעינן מיניה לא פטרי אלא בטומאה אריכתא דלא חזי לאורתא:
Rashi on Pesachim 93b:17:1.english: According to my [opinion] it is not difficult - For even though in [the case of] a distant journey I exempt this one who is fit for the evening, whereas I obligate him in [the case of] one who is ritually impure from a creeping creature, this is the reason: for the Merciful One made the exemption of a ritually pure person dependent on a distant journey, and that is a distant journey — [meaning] that he cannot enter [Jerusalem] at the time of slaughter, for it is written regarding performing [the offering]; and even though he can enter at the time of eating, the Merciful One exempted him. But for a ritually impure person, the Merciful One did not make his exemption dependent on a distant journey, rather on ritual impurity; and the reason for [the exemption of] ritual impurity is because of eating and not because of performing [the offering], for behold he can send his offerings [via an agent]. Furthermore, since [Scripture] wrote "impure from a corpse" and did not write "one who had a seminal emission" or "one who is ritually impure from a creeping creature," we learn from it [that] they only exempt [him] in [the case of] a lengthy impurity where he is not fit for the evening.

Rashi on Pesachim 93b:1:1.hebrew: קסבר מגדף - דכתיב ביה כרת, היינו מברך את השם. וכיון דיש כרת במברך את השם, יליף האי מיניה "נשיאות חטא" "נשיאות חטא" לגזירה שוה:
Rashi on Pesachim 93b:1:1.english: He holds [that] the blasphemer - about whom karet is written, is [the same as] one who blesses the Name. And since there is karet for one who blesses the Name, this [case] derives from it [via] "bearing sin," "bearing sin" for a gezeirah shavah.

Rashi on Pesachim 93b:3:1.hebrew: ורבי נתן - מוקי ליה להאי כי בלשון דהא, וקאי אדלעיל מיניה למיתב טעמא למילתיה: ונכרת בראשון, משום דהא קרבן ה' לא הקריב במועדו בראשון:
Rashi on Pesachim 93b:3:1.english: And Rabbi Natan - [He] interprets this [word] ki in the sense of "because" [deha], and it refers back to what precedes it to give a reason for its statement: [that soul] shall be cut off on the first [Pesach], because "he did not bring the offering of the Lord in its appointed season" on the first [Pesach].

Rashi on Pesachim 93b:4:1.hebrew: לאו היינו מברך את השם - אלא מזמר ומשורר לע"ז, דאיכא דסבירא ליה הכי בכריתות (דף ז:), ולית לן כרת במברך אי לאו מהכא גמירי לה:
Rashi on Pesachim 93b:4:1.english: [The blasphemer] is not [the same as] one who blesses the Name - Rather, [a blasphemer is] one who sings and chants to idolatry, as there is [an opinion] that holds thus in Keritot (7b), and we would not have [the punishment of] karet for one who blesses [the Name] if we did not learn it from here.

Rashi on Pesachim 93b:5:1.hebrew: ורבי חנניא - נמי דריש האי כי לשון אי כר', אלא קסבר לאו מילתא אחריתי היא, אלא כרת דקמא תלא ביה. ונכרת במזיד דראשון, אם קרבן ה' לא יקריב בשני:
Rashi on Pesachim 93b:5:1.english: And Rabbi Ḥananya - [He] also expounds this [word] "ki" as meaning "if," like Rabbi [Yehuda HaNasi], but he holds that it is not another matter; rather, [Scripture] made the karet of the first [Pesach] dependent upon it. And he is cut off for the intentional [omission] of the first, if he does not offer the offering of the Lord on the second [Pesach].

Rashi on Pesachim 93b:6:1.english: As we said - To teach [the penalty of] karet for one who curses [God].

Rashi on Pesachim 93b:7:1.english: All agree [that he is] liable - [To] one karet.

Rashi on Pesachim 93b:8:1.hebrew: לר' ור' נתן חייב - דלא סבירא להו דשני תקנתא דראשון:
Rashi on Pesachim 93b:8:1.english: To Rabbi and Rabbi Natan, [he is] liable - For they do not hold that the second [Pesach] is a rectification for the first [Pesach].

Rashi on Pesachim 93b:9:1.english: [If] one acted unwittingly on the first [Pesach] and intentionally on the second, according to Rabbi he is liable - For he holds [that there is] karet for the second [Pesach] in its own right.

Rashi on Pesachim 93b:9:2.hebrew: לר' נתן ור' חנניא פטור - דהא לא כתיב כרת אלא אראשון, והרי שגג בו:
Rashi on Pesachim 93b:9:2.english: According to Rabbi Natan and Rabbi Chananya, he is exempt - For karet is written only regarding the first [Pesach], and behold, he acted unwittingly regarding it.

Tosafot on Pesachim 93b:12:1.hebrew: עולא לטעמיה - תימה: מנא ליה לעולא דלא הוי שעת שחיטה מתחילת שקיעה? דדם נפסל בשקיעת החמה דריש ליה מ"ביום הקריבו את זבחו", והא קיימא לן בפ' שני דמגילה (דף כ:) דעד צאת הכוכבים יממא הוא:
Tosafot on Pesachim 93b:12:1.english: Ulla [follows] his [own] reasoning - It is astonishing: from where does Ulla know that the time of slaughter is not [valid] from the beginning of sunset [onward]? For [the law that] blood is disqualified at sunset he derives from "on the day he offers his sacrifice," yet we hold in the second chapter of Megillah (20b) that until the emergence of the stars it is [considered] day.

Tosafot on Pesachim 93b:14:1.hebrew: רב יהודה אמר כל שאינו יכול ליכנס בשעת אכילה - תימה, דלרב יהודה, מן המודיעים לא יכול ליכנס בחצי היום וכל הלילה?! ולעולא, בשעת שחיטה — דניחזי אנן! ויש לומר דאיסתתום דרכים, כדאמרינן בר"ה (דף כג:). ועוד, דאליבא דר"ע קיימי' דאית ליה תחומין דאורייתא, ולרב יהודה יכול ליכנס מן המודיעים עד סמוך לתחום בתחלת הלילה, וליכא בינייהו השתא כולי האי; וכן משמע בירושלמי:
Tosafot on Pesachim 93b:14:1.english: Rav Yehuda said: Any [journey from which] one is unable to enter at the time of eating - It is astonishing! According to Rav Yehuda, from Modi'im, could one not enter in half a day and all night?! And according to Ulla, [who says] at the time of slaughter — let us see [for ourselves]! And one can say that the roads are obstructed, as we say in Rosh Hashanah (23b). And furthermore, we are following [the view of] Rabbi Akiva, who holds that [festival] boundary limits [teḥumin] are biblical, and according to Rav Yehuda, one can enter from Modi'im [only] up to near the boundary at the beginning of the night, so there is not so much [difference] between them now; and so it is implied in the Jerusalem Talmud.

Tosafot on Pesachim 93b:15:1.hebrew: וקאמרת שוחטין וזורקין על טמא שרץ - לאלומיה פירכי' הוא דקאמר הכי; ואפי' סבר אין שוחטין, הוה מצי למיפרך מטבול יום, דלכולי עלמא שוחטין וזורקין עליו אע"פ שאינו יכול ליכנס בשעת שחיטה:
Tosafot on Pesachim 93b:15:1.english: "And you say: One slaughters and sprinkles [on behalf of] one who is impure from a creeping animal" - It is in order to strengthen his objection that he said this; and even if he held [that] one does not slaughter [for one impure from a creeping animal], he could have objected from [the case of] a tevul yom, for according to everyone one slaughters and sprinkles on his behalf even though he is unable to enter [the Temple courtyard] at the time of slaughter.

Tosafot on Pesachim 93b:17:1.hebrew: דרך רחוקה לטהור כו' - דתלייה בעשיה, דכתיב: "ובדרך לא היה וחדל לעשות" כו'. ואע"ג דבההוא קרא גופיה כתיב טומאה — "והאיש אשר הוא טהור" — אזלינן בתר אכילה, מדחייב טמא שרץ, דכתיב טמא נפש ולא כתיב טמא שרץ:
Tosafot on Pesachim 93b:17:1.english: "A distant journey [applies] to one who is pure," etc. - For [the verse] made it dependent on the making [of the offering], as it is written: "And was not on a journey, and forbore to make [the Pesach]," etc. And even though in that very same verse impurity is written — "And the man who is pure" — [nevertheless, regarding impurity] we follow [the time of] eating, since [Scripture] obligated one who is impure through a creeping creature, as it is written [that one is deferred if he is] impure through a corpse, and it is not written [one who is] impure through a creeping creature.
